DuckDuckGo Help Guide

The official DuckDuckGo Help Pages, gathered into one document

2026-08-01

DuckDuckGo Help Guide

This guide gathers the official DuckDuckGo Help Pages, published by DuckDuckGo at duckduckgo.com, as they stood on 1 August 2026.

The arrangement is DuckDuckGo’s own. Every help page carries a breadcrumb naming the category it belongs to, and this guide files each article exactly where DuckDuckGo files it. Where DuckDuckGo also places an article in a section beneath that category, the section is named at the top of the article, so its own grouping is not lost.

DuckDuckGo covers several distinct products under one help estate: the search engine, the browser for Mac, Windows, iOS and Android, the browser extensions, Email Protection, the VPN, Personal Information Removal, Identity Theft Restoration and Duck.ai. All of them are here.

What is left out, and why:

  • The DSA transparency reports. These are spreadsheets and a statistical PDF, published under the help pages but not help: they are regulatory filings of numbers, and they convert to nothing readable.
  • Images and icons swept up by the crawl, which hold no text.
  • Twenty-six translations of the Microsoft Ads notice into other languages. The English original is here; the translations say the same thing in Bulgarian, Czech, Danish, German, Greek, Spanish and twenty more.
  • The community forum. DuckDuckGo answers many questions through a community board, which is users talking to one another rather than the publisher’s own documentation.

One thing worth knowing before you read: DuckDuckGo’s help pages are written per-platform, and a single article often covers the Mac browser, the Windows browser, the mobile apps and the browser extension in turn. The steps for your own platform may sit a screen below the heading.

This document holds 19 categories, 282 articles.

Can I donate to DuckDuckGo?

DuckDuckGo has been profitable since 2014, our browsers and extensions have been downloaded over 250 million times, and our private search engine has seen over one hundred billion searches. Because of this, we don’t accept donations.

Instead, you can support us by:

  • Disabling ad blockers so you see our private ads

  • Telling friends and family about DuckDuckGo.

Contact DuckDuckGo

Looking for help or more information about DuckDuckGo features and products? Our existing help pages may already have the info you need: Search, Browser, Email Protection, Sync & Backup, App Tracking Protection, Duck Player, Duck.ai, and more.

  • If you have feedback regarding our search results, or think you’ve encountered results that look suspicious, please use the Share Feedback button located at the bottom of the search results page and follow the prompts. You can also send feedback about specific instant answers where a corresponding feedback option is shown.

  • If you have feedback regarding our browser, please use the Send Feedback option within the browser:

    • Desktop browsers: Open the three-dot menu > Send Feedback

    • Mobile browsers: Open the three-dot menu > Settings > Send Feedback

How does DuckDuckGo make money?

Private ads on our search engine

It is a myth that search engines need to track you to make money. The majority of our revenue is from private ads on our search engine. On most other search engines, ads are based on profiles compiled from your personal information, such as search, browsing, and purchase history. Since we don’t have that information per our Privacy Policy, search ads on DuckDuckGo are based on the search results page you’re viewing instead of being based on who other companies and their tracking algorithms assume you are as a person. For example, if you search for cars, we’ll show you ads about cars. We’ve even created a way to show localized ads while still keeping you completely anonymous. See the Anonymous Localized Results help page for more information on how we do this technically.

Advertising on DuckDuckGo takes the form of sponsored links that appear adjacent to search results. Viewing ads is privacy protected by DuckDuckGo and most ad clicks are managed by Microsoft’s ad network, though even in that case, “Microsoft Advertising does not associate your ad-click behavior with a user profile. It also does not store or share that information other than for accounting purposes.” We have a similar arrangement with TripAdvisor.

This is generally how advertising appears on DuckDuckGo:

If you think you see low-quality ads, for example, ads that seem irrelevant or suspicious, please use the ‘Report Ad’ link for the ad in question on the search results page and follow the prompts.

Visit Advertise on DuckDuckGo Search to learn more about why you should advertise on DuckDuckGo.

Visit Microsoft Advertising to start buying search advertising on DuckDuckGo.

Subscription fees

We also make money from subscription fees. Specifically, the monthly or annual fee that subscribers pay to access the DuckDuckGo subscription, our four-in-one subscription service that includes a VPN, advanced AI models and higher usage limits in Duck.ai, a Personal Information Removal service and an Identity Theft Restoration service.

How does DuckDuckGo protect my privacy?

Quick Answer:

If you’re like most people on the Internet, you use Google to search the web and Google Chrome to browse the web. That means, by default, Google can keep track of every single search you make and website you visit. On those websites, other companies may also track you.

DuckDuckGo is an independent Google alternative that also lets you search and browse the web, but we don’t track your searches or browsing history, and our browsers and extensions help you block other companies from trying to track you. We believe the best way to protect your personal information from hackers, scammers, and privacy-invasive companies is to stop it from being collected at all.

That’s why millions of people choose DuckDuckGo over Chrome and other browsers to search and browse online. Our built-in search engine is like Google but never tracks your searches. And our browsing protections, such as ad tracker blocking and cookie blocking, help stop other companies from collecting your data. Oh, and our browser is free — we make money from privacy-respecting search ads, not by exploiting your data. Plus, DuckDuckGo subscribers get four additional features: a fast and simple VPN, access to advanced AI models in Duck.ai, a Personal Information Removal service, and an Identity Theft Restoration service.

That’s how DuckDuckGo protects your privacy in a nutshell.

Detailed Answer:

Our product vision is to be the “easy button” for online protection.

Our free web browser for Mac, Windows, iOS, and Android allows you to search and browse the internet just like Google search and Chrome, but comes packed with unique privacy protections working behind the scenes to protect and secure your personal information. These overlapping protections work together seamlessly to give you more peace of mind about privacy harms.

We believe the best way to protect your personal information from hackers, scammers, and privacy-invasive companies is to stop it from being collected at all. We do this with a variety of protections:

  • Our private search engine doesn’t track you or your searches. That means unlike Google Search, we don’t save or share your search history, such that we have no way tie your searches or website visits to you personally and we don’t keep profiles of our users.

  • Tracker blocking that goes above and beyond what’s available by default from other browsers like Chrome. For example, our 3rd-party Tracker Loading Protection blocks hidden trackers from companies like Google and Facebook lurking on other websites before they even get a chance to load. This works with our other tracking-preventing features like Cookie Protection, Link Tracking Protection, Referrer Tracking Protection, Fingerprinting Protection, CNAME Cloaking Protection, and Embedded Social Content Tracking Protection to help stop companies from watching what you do online and capturing personal data.

  • Smarter Encryption to ensure that more of the websites you visit and links you click are securely encrypted, relative to other browsers.

  • Cookie Pop-up Protection, which automatically selects the most private option from the cookie consent pop-ups it finds and then hides them.

  • The Fire Button, which allows you to easily burn recent on-device browsing data in one click.

  • Email Protection, which can hide your email address with unique @duck.com addresses when signing up for things online that forward to your existing email address, after removing email trackers.

  • Ad Blocking: Our browser blocks most video ads, including on YouTube. We also prevent 3rd-party trackers from loading, blocking invasive web ads. This not only removes distraction but also helps stop other companies from collecting your data.

  • Duck Player, which opens YouTube videos in a distraction-free theater mode that prevents what you watch from influencing your YouTube recommendations.

  • App Tracking Protection, currently available in our Android browser, that helps block 3rd-party trackers in your other apps, even when you’re not using them.

  • Global Privacy Control (GPC) to help you express your opt-out rights automatically by telling websites (through a header and/or JavaScript-based signal) not to sell or share your personal information.

To be effective, our protections need to continually evolve to mitigate how trackers attempt to evade specific protections. That’s why we offer multiple types of web tracking protections, continually improve them, and work to introduce new and innovative protections.

Note that our private search engine is also independently accessible at duckduckgo.com and as a built-in option in other popular browsers. However, if you just use the search engine, we cannot offer any privacy protection when you visit other web sites. To get that protection, you’ll want our browser or browser extensions. Our help page on web tracking protections details which protections are available on which platforms.

In addition, the DuckDuckGo subscription includes four more features:

  • VPN: Secure your connection anytime, anywhere. Get full-device protection with the VPN built for speed, simplicity, and security. Available on Mac, Windows, iOS, and Android.

  • Advanced AI models in Duck.ai: Chat privately with advanced AI models ideal for complex tasks like coding, problem solving, and reasoning. Subscribers on the Plus plan get access to GPT-5.4 and Claude Sonnet 4.6, and the Pro plan adds Claude Opus 4.8 and 2x higher usage limits than Plus.

  • Personal Information Removal: Find and remove your personal details — like your name and address — from sites that store and sell it, helping to combat identity theft and spam.

  • Identity Theft Restoration: If your identity is stolen, a dedicated advisor will help you restore stolen accounts, recover financial losses, and correct your credit report. Brought to you by Iris (Iris Powered by Generali) — a world leader in identity theft restoration.

Is DuckDuckGo open to partnerships?

For information on ads please go here.

We’re always looking for innovative ways to improve and spread DuckDuckGo. Below lists the main areas where we partner and guidelines for using our technology.

Guidelines

Since we produce our own extensions and apps for the major platforms, we’ve found people increasingly confused as to what was produced by us and what was produced by others. Please follow these guidelines when promoting your applications:

  • Please don’t use DuckDuckGo in the title. (There can be exceptions so please contact us if you think you have a case for doing so). Mentioning us in the description is fine.

  • Please don’t use Dax (our mascot).

  • Please don’t pair our search with something that has another privacy policy, like another auto-complete service that tracks people, as doing so gives users a false sense of privacy.

  • Please don’t include our search results in any sort of frame (whether desktop or mobile) that makes our site embedded within another Web application with the notable exception of browser integration. We simply don’t have the rights to allow framing based on how we generate our search results. For clarity, browser integration where there is an address bar and our site (with branding) takes up the full screen is just fine and encouraged!

  • Please don’t use our URL parameters to strip our branding from our site.

  • Please give us attribution where it makes sense, and where you do link back to the encrypted version of our homepage.

If you have any questions about applying these guidelines in your specific situation, please get in touch.

DuckDuckGo as a Search Option

We have many partnerships with apps, browsers and distributions that include us as a search option:

  • Browsers

  • Linux distributions

  • iOS

  • Android

If you want to add us as a search option, please contact our business development team, as we have some standard ways to easily make this happen.

Get in Touch

We’re always interested in exploring more opportunities but we get a lot of inbound partnership requests, so it helps to be as specific as possible when suggesting a potential partnership. We simply don’t have enough time to do everything right now, and so what we work on has to be compelling. Please send an email to bd@duckduckgo.com.

What is DuckDuckGo?

DuckDuckGo is the independent online protection company for anyone who wants to take back control of their personal information.

We believe the best way to protect your personal information from hackers, scammers, and privacy-invasive companies is to stop it from being collected at all. That’s why millions of people choose DuckDuckGo over Chrome and other browsers to search and browse online. Our built-in search engine is like Google but never tracks your searches, and our browser blocks ads, trackers, and cookies that collect your data. It also offers private, useful and optional AI, including Duck.ai, which lets you chat privately with ChatGPT, Claude, and other AIs, all in one place. Oh, and our browser is free. We make money from privacy-respecting search ads, not by exploiting your data.

In addition, we also offer the DuckDuckGo subscription, a four-in-one subscription service, integrated into our browser. Subscribers get even more protection with three premium features: a fast and simple VPN, access to advanced AI models in Duck.ai, auto-removal of personal information from people-finder sites, and identity restoration if it’s ever stolen.

Take back control of your personal information with the browser designed for data protection, not data collection.

Available for download on Mac, Windows, iOS, and Android.

Learn more about some of the privacy protections built into the DuckDuckGo browser:

  • Our Private Search Engine

  • Web Tracking Protections

  • Email Protection

  • App Tracking Protection

  • Smarter Encryption

  • DuckDuckGo Subscription

All of our products are backed by the same, straightforward Privacy Policy: We don’t track you.

Ad Blocking

About Duck Player

Duck Player is a free feature built into the DuckDuckGo browser for Mac, Windows, iOS, and Android that opens YouTube videos in a distraction-free theater mode and prevents what you watch from influencing your YouTube recommendations.

How does Duck Player work?

Duck Player enforces YouTube’s strictest privacy settings for embedded video, within a clean, theater-like interface. When watching with Duck Player, what you view does not contribute to your personalized YouTube recommendations or your YouTube advertising profile. Note that YouTube can still log video views, so it is not completely anonymous, but your viewing history does not contribute to your personalized recommendations or your YouTube advertising profile.

How do I use Duck Player?

Download the DuckDuckGo browser for Mac, Windows, iOS, or Android and turn on Duck Player in Settings > Ad Blocking > Duck Player. It works directly from DuckDuckGo search results too — just click a YouTube link and choose Duck Player when prompted.

Is Duck Player different from YouTube Ad Blocking?

Yes. Duck Player is the browser’s built-in video player that lets you watch YouTube videos in a distraction-free theater mode. It also protects you from tracking cookies and personalized ads by enforcing YouTube’s strictest privacy settings for embedded video, so what you watch in Duck Player won’t influence your YouTube recommendations.

YouTube Ad Blocking blocks video ads in YouTube videos so you can watch without interruption. It’s the full YouTube experience, just without ads. You can use the browser with both YouTube Ad Blocking and Duck Player enabled.

  • YouTube Ad Blocking in DuckDuckGo Browsers

YouTube Ad Blocking in DuckDuckGo Browsers

When you watch videos in the DuckDuckGo browser, on YouTube or elsewhere, we block ads that appear before and throughout the video.

How does YouTube Ad Blocking work?

To detect and block YouTube ads, we use community-driven filter lists sourced from uBlock Origin. These lists are maintained by an active open-source community and are regularly updated to keep up with changes to how ads are served. We may also apply our own rules to improve compatibility and reduce breakage.

How do I manage YouTube Ad Blocking?

YouTube Ad Blocking is enabled by default for all users. You can turn YouTube Ad Blocking on or off in Settings > Ad Blocking > Block ads on YouTube. You can also turn it on and off while you’re watching a video. On desktop, click the video icon next to the green shield in your address bar. On mobile, tap ☰ > Disable YouTube Ad Blocking. When enabled, ads are removed automatically — there’s nothing else you need to do.

Is YouTube Ad Blocking different from Duck Player?

Yes. YouTube Ad Blocking blocks video ads in YouTube videos so you can watch without interruption. It’s the full YouTube experience, just without ads.

Duck Player is the browser’s built-in video player that lets you watch YouTube videos in a distraction-free theater mode. It also protects you from tracking cookies and personalized ads by enforcing YouTube’s strictest privacy settings for embedded video, so what you watch in Duck Player won’t influence your YouTube recommendations. You can use the browser with both YouTube Ad Blocking and Duck Player enabled.

Can I create images with Duck.ai?

Filed by DuckDuckGo under AI Features, Duck.ai.

Yes, you can use Duck.ai to create AI-generated images. To do so, select “New Image” in Duck.ai and enter a prompt describing the image you want to create. Once your image is generated, you can follow up with additional prompts and describe any changes you’d like to make to the image.

As with chats, there’s a daily limit on the number of images that can be created. DuckDuckGo subscribers have access to higher usage limits than the free version of Duck.ai.

Does Duck.ai have usage limits?

Filed by DuckDuckGo under AI Features, Duck.ai.

Duck.ai is free to use, but there is a daily limit on usage.

Can I pay to increase the usage limit?

DuckDuckGo subscribers on the Plus plan have access to higher usage limits than the free version of Duck.ai. Pro plan subscribers get 2x higher usage limits than the Plus plan.

DuckDuckGo subscription limits.

DuckDuckGo subscribers have two usage limits, a daily and weekly limit, that they can access to suit their needs. Once their daily limit is reached, subscribers can choose to start using their weekly limit to continue their current session. This can be done until the weekly limit is consumed, after which Duck.ai will be unavailable until the weekly limit resets. Daily limits reset at midnight UTC, and weekly limits reset every Sunday at midnight UTC. Current daily and weekly usage can be seen in Duck.ai settings.

Why do I hit a usage limit immediately after starting a conversation?

Due to the way we anonymously enforce usage limits, you may see this error message when using a VPN or cellular network. Try switching VPN locations or switching from a cellular network to WiFi, and see if that resolves the issue. If the issue persists, please use the Share Feedback button at the bottom of the chat page to report it.

Is the method to impose these limits private?

Yes. Per our strict Privacy Policy, “We don’t save your IP address or any unique identifiers alongside your searches or visits to our websites. We also never log IP addresses or any unique identifiers to disk.” The same applies to Duck.ai chats. To impose usage limits, we use a similar method as we do in search to prevent abuse. While we cannot divulge the exact method in order to protect our system from bad actors and misuse, it is engineered in such a way that makes it completely anonymous. For more info on how we manage that technically in other contexts, please see this help page.

Duck.ai

Duck.ai is a feature that allows you to have private conversations with 3rd-party AI chat models, anonymized by us. Anthropic’s Claude 4.5 Haiku, Mistral AI’s Mistral Small 4, OpenAI’s GPT-5.4 nano and GPT-5.4 mini, and gpt-oss-120b and Gemma 4 31B, hosted by Tinfoil.sh, are available to use for free in Duck.ai.

In addition to all of the models available in the free version of Duck.ai, DuckDuckGo subscribers also get access to the additional, advanced AI models. Subscribers on the Plus plan get access to GPT-5.4 and Claude Sonnet 4.6. In addition to the Plus plan models, subscribers on the Pro plan also get Claude Opus 4.8, higher reasoning effort than Plus, and 2x higher usage limits than Plus.

Each model relies on unique algorithms and datasets and will respond to your prompts differently. You can use Duck.ai to get answers to questions, compose an email, summarize text, or just have an interesting conversation. Navigate there directly, or move from traditional search results to ask follow-up questions.

Return to past conversations with Duck.ai’s Recent Chats feature, which stores chats locally on your device – not on DuckDuckGo or other remote servers. Recent chats can be deleted individually or with a click of the Fire Button. You can also pin up to 5 chats to the top of your recent chats list for quick access and to prevent them from being deleted by the Fire Button within Duck.ai.

You can add or remove the Duck.ai button in your DuckDuckGo browser from browser settings, and hide the Duck.ai buttons on the search results page from search settings.

DuckDuckGo’s approach to AI is to provide private, useful, and optional AI features that don’t track how you use them, store your prompts, or train on your data. More information about optional AI-assisted answers on our search engine can be found here.

How does Duck.ai protect my privacy?

Filed by DuckDuckGo under AI Features, Duck.ai.

By default, Duck.ai does not record or store any of your chats, and your conversations are not used to train chat models by DuckDuckGo or the underlying model providers (for example, Open AI and Anthropic). You can choose to share a conversation with us when providing feedback, in which case we store and review it to improve our products. And if you use Sync & Backup, or certain other optional features, your chats are stored in an end-to-end encrypted format that we can’t read.

All chats are anonymized by DuckDuckGo. Metadata that contains personal information (for example, your IP address) is completely removed before prompting the model provider. This means requests to Anthropic, OpenAI, Mistral, Azure, and Tinfoil appear as though they are coming from DuckDuckGo rather than individual users.

In addition, we have agreements in place with all model providers that further limit how they can use data from these anonymous chats.

All Duck.ai model providers agree to:

  • Delete your prompts and responses immediately after generating a reply (called Zero Data Retention or ZDR)

  • Never use your Duck.ai conversations to train their models

  • Never share your data with third parties who may use it for their own commercial purposes (this does not include subprocessors acting on behalf of the model provider)

We allow limited, clearly defined exceptions to these requirements, and we document all of them here.

Images and files are not retained unless flagged as CSAM, in which case they are retained and reported to the relevant authorities (see section below for more details).

  • Tinfoil has the added benefit of using a Trusted Execution Environment, so we are able to ensure, via technical means, that they are unable to read, retain, share, or train on your prompts, responses, or uploads.

Zero provider visibility chat models

Requests to Tinfoil (which hosts gpt-oss-120b and Gemma 4 31B on their servers) are anonymized and, additionally, are processed in a Trusted Execution Environment such that Tinfoil cannot see your prompts or the model’s response. Chat models that support this (currently, gpt-oss-120b and Gemma 4 31B) are labeled “zero provider visibility” in Duck.ai.

You can read the Duck.ai Privacy Policy and Terms of Use here.

How we analyze anonymous chat data

We never store your prompts or any information that could reveal the contents of your conversations (except when you explicitly choose to share a conversation with us when providing feedback). Instead, we use a privacy-preserving system to store anonymous data that allows us to analyze aggregate patterns in Duck.ai chat activity to help understand how the product is being used and where we can improve it.

When you send a message, our servers compute a mathematical representation of it (called an embedding). We use that to match your prompt to a representative prompt from an open-source dataset of chatbot conversations. The embedding of your prompt is held in memory only—never written to disk—and discarded immediately after matching. The matched open-source prompts are what we retain long-term and use to understand aggregate patterns in chat activity.

We also collect aggregate statistics about chat interactions, such as the number of messages in a session, tokens used, or features used. We use this data to monitor performance and understand how Duck.ai is being used. This data is fully anonymized and cannot be connected to any individual user.

How we moderate uploaded images and files

To detect child sexual abuse material (CSAM), images and files you upload are anonymously checked by a third-party content moderation provider, and in some cases, the model provider. No identifying information, other than what might be contained in the uploaded image or file itself, is shared with the content moderation provider (for example, your IP address is not shared). Only uploaded images and files are processed in this way, not text prompts or model responses. Uploaded images and files are not retained unless they are flagged as CSAM, in which case they are retained and reported to the relevant authorities.

This process applies to all models, including those served through Tinfoil. Tinfoil processes prompts and generates model responses in a Trusted Execution Environment, which prevents them from viewing prompts, responses, or uploaded images and files. To perform content moderation in this architecture, your uploaded images and files are sent to the third-party content moderation provider outside of the encrypted channel.

How to choose the best Duck.ai model for your chat

Filed by DuckDuckGo under AI Features, Duck.ai.

Duck.ai offers a variety of AI models from different providers, each with different strengths to perform different types of tasks. Some models are designed for quick, everyday tasks, while others are built to handle more complex work like coding, analysis, or long-form writing.

Each prompt you send in a chat has an associated cost against your usage limit, which resets after regular intervals. More advanced models use more of your limit per prompt, so choosing the right model for the task at hand can help you get the most out of Duck.ai. For simple questions or casual conversations, start with a low- or extra low-cost model. Save high-cost models for more complex tasks that need them.

Some models also support reasoning, which lets the model spend extra effort working through a problem before answering, and “extended reasoning” mode gives the model even more time and compute to think. A good rule of thumb is to use a model that has a reasoning mode if you want a balance between response speed and accuracy, and enable extended reasoning when the prompt you’re asking the model is especially complex or when accuracy matters more than speed. Although models with reasoning can produce better results for complex tasks, they have a higher cost and use more of your usage limit.

Model Comparison

  • Model: Limit CostReasoning Extended Reasoning
  • Claude 4.5 Haiku: Medium ✔
  • Mistral Small 4: Extra Low
  • GPT 5.4 nano: Extra Low ✔
  • GPT 5.4 mini: Low ✔ ✔
  • gpt-oss-120b: Extra Low ✔
  • Gemma 4 31B: Extra Low ✔
  • GPT-5.4*: High ✔ ✔
  • Claude Sonnet 4.6*: High ✔
  • Claude Opus 4.8*: Extra High ✔ ✔

**Requires a* DuckDuckGo subscription

Example Use Cases

Choosing the right model often comes down to matching the complexity of your task to the appropriate cost tier. Here is a general guide to what each tier handles best.

Extra-low-costmodels are best for fast, lightweight tasks where volume or speed matters more than depth. This includes quick brainstorming, simple copy edits, turning bullet points into a short social post, writing or paraphrasing short text, creating simple outlines, and handling straightforward technical tasks like writing spreadsheet formulas or answering quick coding questions.

Low-cost models sit in a useful middle ground, covering tasks that need a bit more reasoning without justifying a higher spend. Good examples include working through homework-style problems, polishing a resume, or comparing a few options before making a decision.

Medium-cost models are well suited for the kinds of writing and communication tasks that come up constantly in a workday, such as drafting emails, summarizing meeting notes, and rewriting a document in a clearer tone.

High-cost models handle more demanding work and tend to split between technical depth and writing quality. This tier is appropriate for debugging tricky code, planning complex projects, analyzing detailed documents with tradeoffs and edge cases, synthesizing research, and turning rough ideas into polished first drafts.

Extra-high-cost models are best reserved for the most open-ended and high-stakes tasks, including deep strategy work, long-form writing that requires nuance and precision, and complex analysis that spans many competing constraints.

Is Duck.ai voice chat and dictation private?

Filed by DuckDuckGo under AI Features, Duck.ai.

As with regular chats in Duck.ai, voice chat and dictation are private, anonymized by us, and not used to train AI models. Audio is not stored by DuckDuckGo or by OpenAI (the model provider for voice chat and dictation) after the chat ends, and we do not use audio to identify you. However, your voice is unique to you and can be a biometric identifier. We want you to understand this risk and make an informed choice before using these features.

How voice chat works

When you start a voice chat, Duck.ai connects you to an OpenAI model through an encrypted relay connection that we cannot decrypt. Your microphone audio is streamed in real time to OpenAI, where the model listens, transcribes what you say, and generates both a spoken and text response. Voice chat is currently available in the DuckDuckGo browser and most 3rd-party browsers (Firefox support coming soon). As with text chats, there’s a daily limit on voice chats. DuckDuckGo subscribers have access to higher usage limits than the free version of Duck.ai.

How dictation works

When you press the microphone icon in Duck.ai to start dictation, Duck.ai will start recording audio locally, for up to 5 minutes per session. Once you stop the recording, the audio file is sent to OpenAI for transcription via DuckDuckGo’s server. OpenAI returns transcribed text to the Duck.ai chat input field, where you can edit it before sending to the model of your choice.

How your voice data is handled

DuckDuckGo protects your audio streams, recordings, and voice data in several ways, to ensure they can only be accessed by OpenAI, (the model provider for voice chat and dictation) and only for the purpose of responding to or transcribing your prompts:

  • Ephemeral processing: Your live audio is streamed only while you’re speaking. Once the your voice chat or dictation session ends, neither DuckDuckGo nor OpenAI keeps recordings of your voice.

  • No training: Your audio and the model’s responses are not used to train AI models.

  • Secure live audio streaming: Voice chat audio streams are encrypted in transit through WebRTC and our relay server.

  • Zero data retention: Neither DuckDuckGo nor OpenAI retains any conversation data after you end a voice chat or dictation session.

About your voice and biometric data

Your unaltered voice is unique to you, meaning it can act as a biometric identifier and could theoretically be used to recognize you. DuckDuckGo does not attempt to identify, fingerprint, or link voices to users, and OpenAI is contractually limited in how they can use voice chat and dictation data to what is necessary to perform their services.

You can always opt out of voice chat or dictation entirely. Even when these features are enabled, your audio is only sent to OpenAI when you initiate a voice chat or dictation session, and is deleted after you end it. To opt-out, go to Duck.ai settings and disable the voice chat and dictation toggles. Once you’ve disabled voice chat or dictation, you’ll need to re-enable them in Duck.ai settings before you can use them again.

Please also see our Duck.ai Privacy Policy

Is my Duck.ai chat history private?

Filed by DuckDuckGo under AI Features, Duck.ai.

Yes! Your chat history in Duck.ai is private, and cannot be accessed by DuckDuckGo or AI chat model providers. Duck.ai offers multiple ways to securely save your chat history. You can save your conversations locally on your device, or on a secure DuckDuckGo server by enabling Sync & Backup.

Chat History

By default, Duck.ai will save your chats locally on your device so you can refer to them later. These chats will appear in the sidebar menu in Duck.ai. You can disable chat history at any time in Duck.ai settings.

In the DuckDuckGo browser on Mac, Windows, iOS, and Android, your Duck.ai chats and settings are stored locally on your device. This means they are stored securely outside of the browser web storage, and they won’t appear in browser developer tools, but they are saved locally and private to you.

Because chats are stored locally on your device, chat retention in non-DuckDuckGo browsers may vary based on the specific browser or app settings. For example, some browsers retain them for extended periods or indefinitely, unless you explicitly clear your browser data. Others, such as Safari, automatically delete your chat history if you go more than 7 days without visiting duck.ai.

Deleting Chat History

When using Duck.ai in the DuckDuckGo browser, deleting your browser data with the Fire Button will not delete Duck.ai chats by default. Instead, you can use the Fire Button within Duck.ai to delete all chats at once.

  • Delete All Chat History: Tap the Fire Button icon at the top of the chats list and choose “Delete Chats”.

  • Delete Multiple Chats: Tap the Fire Button icon at the top of the chats list, then choose “Selected Chats” to reveal the multi-select option for chat deletion. Select the chats you want to delete, and tap the red Fire Button icon at the bottom of the screen to confirm deletion.

  • Delete Individual Chats: Either tap the Fire Button icon beside the chat you want to delete or open the ⋮ menu beside the chat you want to delete and select “Delete Chat”.

  • Delete Pinned Chats: Pinned chats won’t be deleted when you use the Fire Button in Duck.ai. You can unpin them or delete pinned chats individually via the ⋮ menu.

Sync & Backup

Sync & Backup is a free, optional feature that allows you to save more of your conversations privately on a secure DuckDuckGo server, and access them with end-to-end encryption from your browser. With Sync & Backup, the master decryption key is only stored on your devices, so only you can decrypt this information. This means DuckDuckGo never has access to your decryption key and cannot read your chats. You can enable this feature in the DuckDuckGo browser under Settings > Sync & Backup, or in Duck.ai settings in a 3rd-party browser.

Connecting multiple devices to Sync & Backup will merge any Duck.ai chat histories already stored locally on those devices, and keep them in sync. You can connect any device with the DuckDuckGo browser installed to Sync & Backup by going to Settings > Sync & Backup, and selecting “Sync With Another Device.” If you’re using a 3rd-party browser, you can connect it by selecting “Manage” under the Sync & Backup section of Duck.ai Settings, then “Add Another Browser” and following the instructions.

Opting Out of DuckDuckGo AI Features

At DuckDuckGo, we recognize not everyone wants AI in their browser or search results. That’s why all our AI features are optional and can be turned off or tuned down.

Turn off Duck.ai in the DuckDuckGo browser

  2. Turn off Duck.ai to completely disable Duck.ai features in the browser

  1. Go to SearchSettings > AI Features

  2. Turn off Duck.ai

  3. Select Save and Exit to refresh DuckDuckGo search with Duck.ai disabled

Turn off Search Assist

  1. Go to SearchSettings > AI Features

  2. Select Never from the Search Assist dropdown options

  3. Select Save and Exit to refresh DuckDuckGo search with Search Assist disabled

What AI chat models are available?

Filed by DuckDuckGo under AI Features, Duck.ai.

The following models are currently available to use for free in Duck.ai: Anthropic’s Claude 4.5 Haiku, Mistral AI’s Mistral Small 4, OpenAI’s GPT-5.4 nano and GPT-5.4 mini, and gpt-oss-120b and Gemma 4 31B, hosted by Tinfoil.sh.

In addition to all of the models available in the free version of Duck.ai, DuckDuckGo subscribers also get access to the additional, advanced AI models. Subscribers on the Plus plan get access to GPT-5.4 and Claude Sonnet 4.6. In addition to the Plus plan models, subscribers on the Pro plan also get Claude Opus 4.8, higher reasoning effort than Plus, and 2x higher usage limits than Plus. You can change your default chat model at any time by clicking on the current chat model name – in the left sidebar.

Does DuckDuckGo moderate chat responses in any way?

No, we do not filter or modify the responses received from the chat model in any way. As such, responses may contain inaccurate or offensive information. Anthropic, Meta, Mistral, and OpenAI each have their own moderation policies, and you may see those applied when using their models, respectively.

How do I access subscriber-only chat models?

You can access subscriber-only Duck.ai models in any browser, including the DuckDuckGo browser for iOS, Android, Mac, and Windows.

DuckDuckGo Browser

  1. Ensure that the DuckDuckGo browser is running the latest version

  2. Open the three-line menu > Settings

  3. Find DuckDuckGo Subscription and select I Have a Subscription, then follow the prompts

Accessing Duck.ai in other browsers

  1. In your browser, visit Duck.ai

  2. Go to Duck.ai Settings, select I Have a Subscription, then follow the prompts

How do I change chat models?

You can change your chat model by clicking on the current chat model name in the chat input area or by clicking on the reverse-direction arrows icon at the bottom of the current model’s last reply.

What information does Duck.ai share with model providers?

Filed by DuckDuckGo under AI Features, Duck.ai.

In requests to Anthropic, OpenAI, and together.ai (which hosts Mistral on their servers), we share:

  • Today’s date

  • Your timezone

  • Preferred unit system based on global region

We guess your global region using a GEO::IP lookup without saving your actual IP or precise location. Sharing these details helps ensure responses use the right units, reference local dates, and align with your time zone, making answers more accessible and relevant.

Requests to Tinfoil (which hosts gpt-oss-120b and Gemma 4 31B on their servers) also include this information, but are processed on a Trusted Execution Environment (TEE) such that Tinfoil cannot see it.

Learn more about how Duck.ai protects your privacy here.

Do you share any identifiable information with model providers?

No. Duck.ai never passes on any personally identifiable information to AI model providers.

Can Duck.ai know which city I’m in?

Duck.ai can privately share your city-level location with AI model providers to tailor responses without exposing your exact location or IP address. The “Use Approximate Location” setting is optional and turned off by default. You can enable it in Duck.ai settings, and Duck.ai will remember your choice. Turning on “Use Approximate Location” can improve your Duck.ai experience by providing more locally relevant answers.

If you have this setting enabled, Duck.ai simply guesses the city nearest to your location using a GEO::IP lookup. As with search, when you visit our website, your device automatically sends some information to us, like an IP address. We strip out your IP address, so it’s never sent to any of our model providers, including OpenAI, Anthropic, Together.ai, and Microsoft Azure Open. Instead, we provide a city-level location to the instructions we send to model providers, then we throw away both the guesses location and IP address, as per our Privacy Policy, saving none of that info to our server. As with date, timezone, and region information, any city-level location information you choose to send to gpt-oss-120b or Gemma 4 31B are processed on Tinfoil’s TEE and cannot be seen by Tinfoil.

App Tracking Protection

Does App Tracking Protection block trackers in all my apps?

App Tracking Protection is a feature in the DuckDuckGo Private Browser for Android that helps block 3rd-party trackers in your apps, even when you’re not using them. We aim to protect your privacy as much as possible, but no service can eliminate all hidden app tracking or profiling. To be effective, App Tracking Protection needs to continually evolve to mitigate how trackers attempt to evade us without disrupting essential usability. Some apps depend on code delivered by 3rd-party trackers to function and blocking these trackers can cause apps to behave unexpectedly.

To preserve essential usability, we may make limited exceptions and automatically disable protection for individual apps. For example, we automatically disable protection for browsers and other apps that load websites so content appears normally.

In other cases, we can preserve essential usability by making limited exceptions for individual trackers while leaving protection enabled for apps. For example, if blocking a certain 3rd-party tracker in a mobile game prevented players from receiving in-game rewards, we may make a limited exception for that tracker within the game app, while continuing to block the tracker in other apps.

We also don’t block trackers belonging to an app’s parent company (known as 1st-party trackers) because doing so would likely cause the app to behave unexpectedly. This means that protection may be automatically disabled for apps like those installed by default on your Android device.

If you think App Tracking Protection might be causing usability issues in one of your apps, you can manually disable protection for apps in Settings > App Tracking Protection > Manage > View Apps and report the issue you experienced to us. We review user-reported app issues daily, and work to address them continuously by updating our open source list of app trackers and exceptions like those described above to preserve usability.

  • What is DuckDuckGo App Tracking Protection?
  • How does DuckDuckGo App Tracking Protection work?
  • Is App Tracking Protection a VPN?

How does DuckDuckGo App Tracking Protection work?

App Tracking Protection is a feature in the DuckDuckGo Private Browser for Android that helps block 3rd-party trackers in your apps, even when you’re not using them. App Tracking Protection detects when other apps on your phone are about to send data to any of the 3rd-party tracking companies in our list of app trackers. For example, when Facebook tries to track you in a health app. Our protection works to block tracking requests that occur over HTTPS, which includes the majority of app traffic on the Internet.

We continually work to keep our app tracker blocklist up to date by identifying new app trackers and mitigating how trackers attempt to evade us. When we update our list, your App Tracking Protection will update automatically.

  • What is DuckDuckGo App Tracking Protection?
  • Does App Tracking Protection block trackers in all my apps?
  • Is App Tracking Protection a VPN?

Is App Tracking Protection a VPN?

App Tracking Protection is a feature in the DuckDuckGo Private Browser for Android that helps block 3rd-party trackers in your apps, even when you’re not using them. Though similar, App Tracking Protection is different from a VPN.

App Tracking Protection works locally on your device, sitting between your apps and the servers they talk to. When App Tracking Protection recognizes a tracker on our list of app trackers, it blocks the tracker from sending personal information (such as your IP address, activity, and device details) off your device. All other traffic reaches its destination, so your apps work normally.

A VPN is different. It works by establishing a secure, encrypted connection (VPN tunnel) between your device and one of its servers. All device network traffic that passes through this tunnel is anonymized and hidden from your Internet service provider and other websites you visit.

The DuckDuckGo VPN works in the same way, and secures your connection across your entire device, including your apps and browsers, on up to five devices at once. Plus, it has a strict no-logging policy, and you can connect in just a click, directly from the DuckDuckGo browser. Learn more

Is my data private?

Yes. As explained above, App Tracking Protection just works on your device and doesn’t send your personal data off your device to DuckDuckGo or other companies.

If not a VPN, then why does App Tracking Protection use a VPN connection?

You will be asked to set up a virtual private network (VPN) connection, but you don’t need to install a VPN app for App Tracking Protection to work.

This permission allows App Tracking Protection, which just works locally on your device, to monitor network traffic so that it can block trackers on our list.

Will App Tracking Protection work if I also use a VPN app?

App Tracking Protection is only compatible with the DuckDuckGo VPN. Because Android only allows one active VPN connection per device, App Tracking Protection won’t work with other VPNs. However, the DuckDuckGo VPN can share the same VPN connection because both features are managed by the DuckDuckGo browser.

If using a different VPN, we recommend that you enable App Tracking Protection when you are not using other VPNs. Just make sure your VPN app isn’t set to “Always-on.” Go to Android Network settings > VPN. Then, check the gear icon for any listed VPN apps and disable “Always-on.” Some VPN apps may also have an auto-connect setting which must be disabled.

DuckDuckGo Subscription

Am I able to manually choose the VPN server location?

Filed by DuckDuckGo under DuckDuckGo Subscription, Most Common Questions.

Am I able to manually choose the VPN server location?

Yes, you can switch locations manually. By default, you will connect to the closest available server in your country. If a server is not available in your country, you will connect to the next closest server to you.

You can also choose to override the default selection and select from any one of our available locations by tapping or clicking on VPN Settings from the in-app VPN menu.

Are smart home devices and voice assistants affected by VPN?

Filed by DuckDuckGo under DuckDuckGo Subscription, Most Common Questions.

Are smart home devices and voice assistants affected by VPN?  

The DuckDuckGo VPN is only available on Android, macOS, iOS, and Windows devices that are compatible with the DuckDuckGo app. It is not compatible with smart home devices, dedicated voice assistant devices, router VPN configurations, or other similar internet connected devices at this time.

On Android, macOS, and iOS, the VPN automatically excludes local devices on your network so you can still access connected devices like a home printer or smart thermostat while the VPN is connected. We do not yet offer the ability to exclude local traffic on the Windows app, but we hope to do so soon.

Are text messages protected through VPN?

Filed by DuckDuckGo under DuckDuckGo Subscription, Most Common Questions.

Are text messages protected through VPN?

SMS text messages are typically transmitted through the control channel of your cellular network. In this case, they would not be protected with any VPN.  

However, there are some messaging apps that use other technologies to transmit through mobile data (such as WhatsApp or Signal). In these cases, text messages would be protected with a VPN.

Are video/voice calls protected through VPN?

Filed by DuckDuckGo under DuckDuckGo Subscription, Most Common Questions.

Are video/voice calls protected through VPN?

Video calls are protected through VPN, as they run through mobile data or Wi-Fi. Voice calls are protected if your device uses VoIP and/or Wi-Fi calling.

Not at this time, unfortunately. You will need to cancel your current subscription and then purchase a new subscription with the new pay period that you prefer.

Can my personal information reappear after it is removed?

Yes, personal info can reappear on people-search sites if it’s collected from new sources. We re-scan sites regularly to ensure your information is promptly removed if it appears again.

Do any of these providers see my prompts?

Filed by DuckDuckGo under DuckDuckGo Subscription, Most Common Questions.

Model providers need to see your prompts in order for their models to provide responses. However, before your prompts are sent to the model providers, DuckDuckGo removes any metadata that contains personal information (for example, your IP address), and sends the prompt via DuckDuckGo’s servers. This means that prompts appear as though they are coming from DuckDuckGo rather than individual users.

This help page has more information on how we make Duck.ai private and anonymous.

DuckDuckGo Subscription Payments

What payment methods are accepted?

If you subscribe from a DuckDuckGo browser downloaded from the Google Play Store or Apple App Store, they handle the payments directly — accepting any payment method associated with your app store account. Their respective privacy policies and terms of service apply to payment processing.

If you’re a US resident and you subscribe from our website, or from a DuckDuckGo browser downloaded from our website, we use Stripe as a payment processor. You can use a prepaid credit card to enhance your privacy when subscribing via Stripe, but only U.S. credit cards are accepted, as this payment option is only available to U.S. residents at this time. Like your searches and browsing activity, we do not store your payment info, and it cannot be tied to your activity within DuckDuckGo.

How do I upgrade, downgrade, or cancel my subscription?

Where you can manage your subscription or payment method depends on the platform on which you subscribe:

  • If you subscribed via the Apple App Store, you can manage your subscription and payment method in the Apple App Store on an Apple device signed into your Apple account. Open the Settings app, search for Subscriptions, and then click “DuckDuckGo Subscription”.

  • If you subscribed via Google Play Store, you can manage your subscription and payment method in the Google Play Store on an Android device signed into your Google account. Open the Google Play app, tap your profile picture, tap Payments and Subscriptions, tap Subscriptions, then tap “DuckDuckGo Subscription”.

  • If you subscribed via our website or via the DuckDuckGo browser downloaded from our website, you can manage your subscription and payment method through the browser under the 3-line menu > Settings > Subscription Settings > Update Plan or Cancel. If you don’t have the DuckDuckGo browser, you can cancel your subscription here: 0

If you cancel your subscription, it will remain active through its current billing period, but it will not automatically renew.

Upgrading to a higher plan (e.g., Plus to Pro)

Your new plan starts immediately. Through the Google Play Store and our payment processor, Stripe, you’ll be charged the difference in price for the remainder of your current billing period — any unused time on your old plan is credited toward the new one. Through the Apple App Store, you will be charged the full amount of the upgraded subscription, and a prorated refund of your original plan will be issued by Apple.

Downgrading to a lower plan (e.g., Pro to Plus)

Your current plan stays active until the end of your billing period, and the lower plan takes effect when the next cycle begins. You won’t be charged again until then.

Switching billing frequency (e.g., monthly to annual, or vice versa)

The new billing rate takes effect at the start of your next billing cycle.

Can I add or delete a payment method?

How you manage the payment method of your subscription depends on the platform used to subscribe:

  • To add or delete a payment method from the Google Play Store, go to your Google Play account settings, select “Payment methods,” and then choose the option to add a new payment method or remove an existing payment method. Then follow the prompts.

  • To add or delete a payment method in the Apple App Store, open the Settings app, tap on “Payment & Shipping,” and follow the prompts to add a new payment method or remove an existing one. You may need to sign in to your Apple Account to make these changes.

  • To add or delete a payment method in our payment processor, Stripe, you can click here to access your subscription account linked to your email address. From there, you should have options to add new payment method or delete an existing one. NOTE: Stripe requires at least one payment method linked to an active subscription, so you may need to add a new payment method before deleting an old credit card.

How do I check when my subscription expires?

Your subscription will auto-renew monthly or annually, depending on the payment terms selected, until canceled. The renewal or expiration date (if you’ve canceled) is available in the DuckDuckGo Subscription settings section within the DuckDuckGo browser.

Do I need to share personal information to subscribe to DuckDuckGo?

You don’t need to share any personal information with DuckDuckGo in order to subscribe. We believe the best way we can protect your personal information is to not collect it at all.

We don’t keep logs of your VPN activity, your Duck.ai chats are private and never used to train AI, and information you submit for Personal Information Removal is stored on your device, not on our servers. Similarly, we don’t process payments, which is done by either Stripe, the Apple App Store, or Google Play Store, depending on how you subscribe.

In addition, you don’t need to create an account in order to subscribe. Instead, and to protect your identity even further, we assign a random ID to your subscription that we use to activate your subscription on your devices. This random ID is not connected to any of your subscription activity or payment information. If you opt to add an email address for ease of activation, it also won’t be connected to your subscription activity or payment information.

What happens to my data after I cancel my subscription?

If you choose to cancel your subscription, we will delete any personal information we have (for example, your email address) within 30 days, unless we are legally required to keep it longer.

I have a question not covered here, how can I get help?

Please contact support via our subscriber support form. We use Zendesk, a third-party customer support platform, to store and facilitate our responses to support requests. DuckDuckGo representatives, and in some cases, representatives from our customer support vendor will review and address your support requests. These representatives may be located outside your jurisdiction, as described in the Privacy Policy.

If you have ideas on how to improve the subscription, please let us know using the “Share Feedback” button in the DuckDuckGo browser.

Getting Started With The DuckDuckGo Subscription

As soon as you complete the purchase for your DuckDuckGo subscription (available on iOS, Android, Mac, and Windows), you can start taking advantage of its included services immediately on the device on which you subscribed (a.k.a. your initial device).

NOTE: Due to our strict Privacy Policy, we intentionally collect as little personal information as possible during the subscription process. All of the initial authentication requests to activate your subscription are done using secure tokens, and without any personal information, such as your email address. Only if you choose to activate your subscription on an additional device, will our system require your email address for authentication.

Subscription Settings

All the services offered through the DuckDuckGo subscription are managed directly within the DuckDuckGo browser on your device(s). To access these settings, open the 3-line menu in the browser > Settings. This takes you to DuckDuckGo browser settings.

From within the DuckDuckGo Settings screen, on the left menu panel, go to Subscription Settings.

Add Your Subscription to Other Devices

You do not need to add your email address to your subscription. It’s only necessary if you would like to activate your DuckDuckGo subscription on one or more additional devices.

💡 Before you can use your subscription on other devices, you need to add your email address to your subscription on the device where you initially subscribed.

When you add your email address, DuckDuckGo will send a one-time passphrase (OTP) for authentication purposes. This OTP will be 4 randomly generated words separated by spaces, and all lower-case. This OTP will need to be entered, exactly as written, into the designated field in the DuckDuckGo browser.

Once you’ve manually authenticated your email address, you will see it displayed on the Subscription Settings screen. If you need to make any changes to the email address you can use the “Edit” button.

To activate your subscription on an additional device, you can go to this Subscription Settings screen on the additional device, and add the same email address, following the same authentication process described above, but using a different one-time passphrase.

Subscription Settings

This Subscription Settings section is displayed when your subscription is set to renew. If you purchased directly through the DuckDuckGo website, and not through an app store, you also have the ability to update your plan (e.g., change from monthly to annual renewal) or cancel your subscription. If you purchased your subscription through the Google Play Store or the Apple App Store, you can manage your subscription through the respective store.

❗If you purchased directly through a store (Google Play Store or Apple App Store), your DuckDuckGo subscription is neither managed, nor renewed through DuckDuckGo. We do not have any record of your subscription, so any cancellations or changes to your subscription must be done through the store.

In some cases, you may need to remove the DuckDuckGo subscription from a device. This can be done by selecting the “Remove From This Device” link. Removing the subscription from your device will result in you not being able to access the services offered through the subscription (e.g., the VPN, Personal Information Removal, etc.) on that specific device, while still maintaining an active subscription. Removing a subscription from a device does not cancel the subscription.

Set up the VPN

To set up the DuckDuckGo VPN on your initial device, open the 3-line menu in the DuckDuckGo browser > Settings > VPN, and then select the option to “Install.”

If you’d like to set up the VPN on an additional device, you will first need to activate the DuckDuckGo Subscription (using the OTP steps listed in Add Your Subscription to Other Devices), and then you’ll have access to the VPN screen in the browser settings.

Connect the VPN to a server location

Once the DuckDuckGo VPN is set up, you will have the option to “Open VPN…”. By default, the VPN will connect to the DuckDuckGo server location physically closest to your device, but you can manually change it to be any of the server locations we have available.

💡 Connecting to a VPN server that’s located closest to you will ensure the fastest possible internet speeds. Although you can connect to a VPN server located halfway around the world, speeds will be impacted, as all your internet traffic will need to travel all that way, back and forth, to request and load website and app data.

Set up your Personal Information Removal profile

In order for Personal Information Removal (PIR) to effectively scan and remove your personal data from online broker sites, you must first configure your PIR profile. To do so, open the 3-line menu in the DuckDuckGo browser > Settings > Personal Information Removal.

Personal Information Removal can be configured for only one person. Enter the full name, including maiden name and any nicknames, if applicable. Being as complete as possible will help to maximize results. Next, enter the birth year and the cities lived in, then save the profile. This data is stored locally on your device and never shared with DuckDuckGo.

💡 PIR will run its scan and removal processes in the background. You do not need to keep the DuckDuckGo browser open for the processes to function.

Recovering from a stolen identity

Your DuckDuckGo Subscription also includes Identity Theft Restoration, which can help you get back on the right track if your identity is ever stolen.

To open a case, open the 3-line menu in the DuckDuckGo browser > Settings > Identity Theft Restoration and select “Talk to an Advisor.” A randomly generated Access Code will be displayed, and you will need to provide that to the advisor when you call the number presented on the screen.

How can I exclude apps or websites from the VPN?

Filed by DuckDuckGo under DuckDuckGo Subscription, Most Common Questions.

How can I exclude apps or websites from the VPN?

Some apps and websites do not function properly when they detect a connection over VPN. As a workaround, you can bypass the VPN and exclude apps and/or websites.

To configure VPN exclusions, open the three-line menu in the DuckDuckGo browser, go to Settings > VPN. From there, you can select the Excluded Apps and/or Excluded Websites (not currently available on Android) and specify the apps/websites you want to exclude from the VPN.

How can I get Personal Information Removal services outside the US?

Our Personal Information Removal offering is only available in the U.S., where data collection without consent is not restricted.

How do I activate my subscription in Duck.ai in 3rd-party browsers?

Filed by DuckDuckGo under DuckDuckGo Subscription, Most Common Questions.

If you purchased your subscription on one device (Purchase Device) and are trying to activate your subscription in a 3rd-party browser (Second Browser) you need to follow the steps below:

First, you need to add an email address to the subscription, on the Purchase Device

  1. In the DuckDuckGo browser, under Subscription Settings, click on ‘Add to Another Device’

  2. Click ‘Add email’

  3. Enter an email address (this can be any email address that you have access to)

  4. Within a minute or so you’ll receive a One-Time-Passphrase to that email address

  5. Copy and Paste the passphrase into the page on the Purchase Device

    • You only have 5 minutes to enter this code or it will expire

    • If you are typing it, make sure that auto-correct doesn’t change the words

  6. Success - you’ve just added an email address to your subscription

    • There are two ways to confirm this:

      • You should receive an email with the subject ‘Your email has been added to your subscription’

      • If you follow the steps above, at step #2 you should see your email address displayed

Second, you need to activate your subscription using the email address, in the Second Browser

  1. In the Second Browser, navigate to Duck.ai

  2. Click on the settings icon

  3. Click “I have a Subscription”

  4. Enter the email address you added on the Purchase Device

  5. Within a minute or so you’ll receive a One-Time-Passphrase to that email address

  6. Copy and Paste the passphrase into the Second Browser

    • You only have 5 minutes to enter this code or it will expire

    • If you are typing it, make sure that auto-correct doesn’t change the words

  7. Success - You have activated your subscription on the Second Browser, you can now activate your subscription on all your devices using the same email address

How do I activate the subscription on another device?

Filed by DuckDuckGo under DuckDuckGo Subscription, Most Common Questions.

Initial Device

In order to activate the subscription on an additional device, you must ensure that your email address has been manually added to the subscription on the device that was used to initially purchase the subscription. This device is known as the initial device.

💡 The email address must be the same one used when you purchased the subscription (e.g., the one linked to your Google account signed into the Play Store on your Android device, or your Apple Account signed in to the App Store)

  1. Open the DuckDuckGo browser on the initial device and open the 3-line menu > Settings.

  2. Under Subscription Settings, go to “Add to Another Device”.

  3. Select “Add email” and enter your email address linked to the account that purchased the subscription (e.g., the Google account on an Android device, or the Apple Account on an iPhone, etc.).

  4. DuckDuckGo will send a one-time passphrase (OTP) for authentication purposes. This OTP will be 4 randomly generated words separated by spaces, and all lower-case letters.

  5. This OTP will need to be entered, exactly as written, into the designated field in the DuckDuckGo browser on the initial device. Note: this step is time-sensitive, as the OTP expires after 5-10 minutes.

Additional Device  

Once you’ve successfully authenticated your email address on the initial device, and it has been manually linked to your subscription, you can then activate the subscription on an additional device.

  1. Open the DuckDuckGo browser on the additional device and open the 3-line menu > Settings.

  2. Under Subscription Settings, go to “Add to Another Device”.

  3. Select “I Have a Subscription” and follow the steps to enter the same email address linked to the subscription (added in step 3 on the initial device).

  4. DuckDuckGo will send a one-time passphrase (OTP) for authentication purposes. This OTP will be 4 randomly generated words separated by spaces, and all lower-case letters.

  5. This OTP will need to be entered, exactly as written, into the designated field in the DuckDuckGo browser on the initial device. Note: this step is time-sensitive, as the OTP expires after 5-10 minutes.

  6. Once the passphrase is entered correctly, your subscription will be activated on your additional device.

How do I know that the VPN is connected and working?

Filed by DuckDuckGo under DuckDuckGo Subscription, Most Common Questions.

How do I know that the VPN is connected and working?

The easiest way to check the status of the DuckDuckGo VPN is by navigating to the VPN screen in the DuckDuckGo app. Depending on the operating system of your device, there are also ways to quickly check the VPN status outside of the app too.  

Here’s what to look for:  

  1. Mobile devices: Look for the key icon (Android) or the “VPN” label (iOS) at the top of your screen. On iOS, the “VPN” label is only visible from the Control Center.

  2. Desktop devices: Look for the DuckDuckGo VPN “globe” icon in the top-right menu bar (macOS) or the bottom-right taskbar menu (Windows). If the VPN is connected, you will see a small green lock on the globe icon.

Additionally, most operating systems have system settings for VPNs that display all the installed VPNs on that device. You can also check the status of each VPN there.  

To check that the VPN is working correctly when on, open a new tab in the DuckDuckGo browser and search, “What is my IP?” Confirm that the displayed IP address and location matches the one displayed in the VPN menu. You can then disable the VPN and repeat this search to confirm that your IP address and location revert back to your real IP address and location once the VPN is turned off.

How do I turn off autocomplete?

If you’re referring to the autocomplete suggestions on duckduckgo.com when searching, you can turn this off by going to 0 and turning off “Autocomplete Suggestions”. 

If you’re referring to the suggestions when performing a search in the DuckDuckGo mobile app, you can turn this off by going to Settings > Private Search and then turning off “Autocomplete Suggestions” and/or “Recently Visited Sites”.

How long does it take for my personal information to be removed?

Filed by DuckDuckGo under DuckDuckGo Subscription, Most Common Questions.

How long does it take for my personal information to be removed?

The time it takes to remove your information varies from site to site. Some sites process removal requests within 24 hours, while others can take up to 6 weeks.   

Sometimes there are instances where results “get stuck”. When this happens, there may be a need to either take additional actions or go through a waiting period before resubmitting a removal request.  

Rest assured, Personal Information Removal is designed to follow each site’s process and ensure your personal information is properly removed.

How to activate a DuckDuckGo subscription after purchase

As soon as you complete the purchase for your DuckDuckGo subscription (available on iOS, Android, Mac, and Windows), you can start taking advantage of its included services immediately on the device on which you subscribed (a.k.a. your initial device).

Although the subscription is intended for personal, individual use, you can activate it on other devices to use the VPN and access advanced models in Duck.ai.

💡 If you want to activate your subscription on more than your initial device, you will need to provide an email address for authentication. To do this, on both your initial device and any additional devices, follow the steps below.

Add your subscription to other devices

If you’re in the DuckDuckGo browser:

  1. If you’re in the DuckDuckGo browser, open the three-line menu next to the address bar.

  2. Go to Settings > Subscription Settings

  3. Select I Have a Subscription, then follow the prompts to add the email address you already added to your initial device.

If you’re using Duck.ai in a different browser:

  1. Open the Settings & More option in the sidebar panel.

  2. Go to Settings > I Have a Subscription, then follow the prompts to add the email address you already added to your initial device.

When you add your email address, DuckDuckGo will send a one-time passphrase (OTP) for authentication purposes. This OTP will be 4 randomly generated words separated by spaces, and all lower-case. This OTP will need to be entered, exactly as written, into the designated field in the DuckDuckGo browser.

Once you’ve manually authenticated your email address, you will see it displayed on the Subscription Settings screen. If you need to make any changes to the email address you can use the “Edit” button.

Do I need the DuckDuckGo browser to use my subscription?

The VPN and Personal Information Removal are configured and managed through the DuckDuckGo browser. So, in order to set up and maintain those features, the DuckDuckGo browser is required. However, advanced models for Duck.ai can be accessed from any browser with an activated subscription.

The DuckDuckGo browser lets you search and browse privately, with more than a dozen privacy features in one convenient package, all for free. By adding a DuckDuckGo subscription, you can encrypt Internet connections across your entire device (even outside the browser) with our VPN; chat with advanced AI models in Duck.ai; limit the visibility of your personal info online and data brokers’ access to it with Personal Information Removal; and, with Identity Theft Restoration, we can help get you back on track should you become a victim of identity theft.

You can access your subscription on any device with the DuckDuckGo browser installed. First, download the DuckDuckGo browser (or update to the latest version), then follow the instructions for your device.

How to change your DuckDuckGo subscription plan

You can switch between the DuckDuckGo subscription’s Plus or Pro plan at any time by following these steps:

In the DuckDuckGo browser

  1. Go to Settings > DuckDuckGo Subscription

  2. Select View All Plans

  3. Select the plan you’d like to switch to and proceed to payment or confirm

In 3rd-party browsers

  1. Navigate to Duck.ai

  2. Go to Settings & More > Manage Subscription

  3. Select View All Plans

  4. Select the plan you’d like to switch to and proceed to payment or confirm

How to Send Crash Reports on iOS

Filed by DuckDuckGo under DuckDuckGo Subscription, Most Common Questions.

To send a copy of a recent crash report of the DuckDuckGo browser on iOS, please follow these steps:

  1. Open Settings > Privacy & Security > Analytics & Improvements (iOS 16 and newer)

  2. Tap Analytics Data

  3. Scroll down alphabetically to find the the most recent log beginning with “DuckDuckGo” (the end of the log name has the date and time that the crash occurred)

  4. Tap the desired log

  5. Tap the Share icon, and select your preferred method to share the crash report (e.g., as an attachment in an email to Support)

How to Send Crash Reports on macOS

Filed by DuckDuckGo under DuckDuckGo Subscription, Most Common Questions.

To send a copy of a recent crash report of the DuckDuckGo browser on macOS, please follow these steps:

  1. Click the Finder icon in your Dock, then Applications > Utilities > Console

  2. Click Crash Reports from the left sidebar

  3. Locate the most recent crash reports from “DuckDuckGo” in the list (logs are listed alphabetically)

  4. Right-click the desired log’s file name, and select Reveal in Finder

  5. Attach the selected file to an email and send to Support

How to Send Crash Reports on Windows

Filed by DuckDuckGo under DuckDuckGo Subscription, Most Common Questions.

To send a copy of a recent crash report of the DuckDuckGo browser on Windows, please follow these steps:

  1. Right-click on the Start button and select Event Viewer

  2. In the left pane, expand Windows Logs and select Application

  3. In the center pane, look for the recent logs with the Source “DuckDuckGo” or “Application Error” that reference DuckDuckGo

    • Tips to narrow things down, you can try the following:

      • Filter the logs by right-clicking Application > Filter Current Log…, selecting “Error” for the Level, and limiting to the last 12 hours

      • In the File menu, click Edit > Find… (or Ctrl + F) to search for “DuckDuckGo” across all entries

  4. Once you’ve found the relevant entries, use Save All Events As… to export a 0 file, or right-click an entry and copy the XML Details, then send the file as an attachment or copy the details of the entry in an to Support
